# Profiling your own code

@difference Extension: [Microseconds](Microseconds) times in millionths of a second, and `--profile` with the `Profile*` commands measures the parts of a program and of the runtime.

## Timing with Microseconds

[MilliSecs](MilliSecs) counts whole milliseconds, so a single frame time of a program that runs faster than about 60 frames per second is off by up to 1 ms, adding up such frame times keeps the rounding noise, and a frame time of 0 breaks any division by it. Use [Microseconds](Microseconds) for this. It works in every program, needs no option, and returns a `UInt64`; subtract before converting so that nothing is lost:

```blitzbasic
start:UInt64 = Microseconds()
Delay 20
elapsed:UInt64 = Microseconds() - start
Print "took " + (Float(elapsed) / 1000.0) + " ms"
```

* A variable without a type is an `Int` and keeps only 32 bits, so declare the times with `:UInt64`.
* Take the score or frame rate of a benchmark from one start and one end divided by the number of frames, not from the average of single frame times.
* The clock does not follow the system time. How finely it ticks depends on the system, so time many frames or repeats instead of trusting one tiny difference.

## Timing parts of a program

`ProfileBegin "name"` and `ProfileEnd "name"` time a part of the program and add it to the runtime's list of timers. They only do something in a program compiled with `--profile` (or `-d`) and are empty calls otherwise, so they can stay in a release.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 64, 64, 0, 2
For i = 1 To 10
	ProfileBegin "ai"
	Delay 2 ; the part that is measured
	ProfileEnd "ai"
	Cls
	Flip
	Print "ai took " + ProfileValue("ai") + " ms"
Next
```

* A key is a name of your own (not case sensitive, up to 63 characters, at most 64 keys, and not the name of a runtime item, see [ProfileItemName](ProfileItemName)).
* The numbers are per frame, from one `Flip` to the next: a part that runs 200 times in a frame gives the sum. [ProfileValue](ProfileValue) gives the frame that ended with the last `Flip`, in milliseconds as a `Float`, and 0 before the first full frame or for an unknown key.
* Keys are independent timers, so an outer part includes the time of the parts inside it. The same key can not be nested in itself.
* The time is wall time, so waiting in `Delay` shows up. [ProfileEnable](ProfileEnable) `0` stops the timers, for example while loading.

## What the runtime measures

Compile with `--profile` (or `-d`). The runtime then times `UpdateWorld`, animation, `RenderWorld` and its parts, `Flip`, `Delay`, the wait for the GPU and the GPU passes. Turn the report on with `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_FPS=1` or [ProfileFPS](ProfileFPS) `1`; it prints once a second to the error output or the file of [ProfileOutput](ProfileOutput):

```text
cpu: x86_64 v3: sse3 ssse3 ...
fps: 497, submits: 497, waiting: 12.4 ms
  gpu thread: vkQueueSubmit 20.1 ms, vkQueuePresentKHR 3.2 ms, frames that had to be waited for 0
  gpu passes: scene 610.2 ms, 2d 32.5 ms, copy 10.1 ms, present 4.0 ms, frame 702.7 ms
  UpdateWorld: 41.0 ms
  RenderWorld: 480.3 ms
  Flip: 120.8 ms
  ai: 83.4 ms
```

* Every number is the **total for that second in milliseconds**, not per frame: divide by `fps`.
* Indented parts of `RenderWorld` (lights+cameras, collect, draws, sort+group, record commands) are included in it; do not add them up again. `clusters for GPU culling` is part of `draws`.
* A large `waiting` means the program is limited by the GPU. The GPU passes come back a frame or two late and run next to the CPU, so they do not add up with the CPU timers.
* If the program is vsynced (`Flip 1`), `Flip` contains the wait for the display and `fps` is the refresh rate. Use `Flip 2` or `Flip 0` to measure how fast it can go, see [Flip](Flip#flip-2).

A single slow frame disappears in these totals. [ProfileSlow](ProfileSlow) `milliseconds` (or `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_SLOW`) lists such frames one by one with where their time went; only timers of at least 0.5 ms are listed. To use the numbers inside the program, use `ProfileValue` with the names from `ProfileItemName`, for example `ProfileValue("RenderWorld: draws")`.

## Comparing two versions

Compile both the same way and run them several times on the same machine; a difference smaller than the spread between runs of one build is noise. Use `Flip 2` or `Flip 0`, a window of fixed size, and name the GPU on a machine that has more than one. The timers are for finding where the time goes; take the final comparison from a release build with `Microseconds()`.

On Windows, [ProfileSample](ProfileSample) `"file"` (or `BLITZLLVM_PROFILE_SAMPLE=file`) samples where the program spends its time in a `--profile` program, with call stacks when built with `-g`; see [Environment variables](Environment-Variables).
